events.title: Trinity's Hotel Escape
events.summary: Police breach a hotel room and take Trinity into custody, but she kills the squad in seconds and flees. As Agents Smith, Brown and Jones seize jurisdiction over the operation, Trinity fights her way up through the building and across the rooftops — pursued by an Agent who matches her impossible jumps — before hurling herself through a window, surviving the fall, and answering a ringing payphone an instant before a truck obliterates the booth. She escapes, but the Agents recover from the failure by confirming their informant is real and seizing the name of the crew's next target, 'Neo,' then launching a search.
events.action: Trinity is arrested at gunpoint, detonates the arrest into a firefight she wins, runs a building-and-rooftop pursuit against the Agents, and exits through a payphone as the Agents convert the failed capture into the lead that turns them from hunted to hunter.

registers.entry: Cornered in Room 303, hands on the keyboard, surrounded by an armed squad.
registers.change: custody: detained -> at large, then hunted through the building, across the rooftops, and out to the street
registers.exit: Escaped via a payphone, gone before the booth is destroyed; physically separated from all pursuers.

registers.entry: Uninjured, in full control of her body.
registers.change: condition: whole -> wounded (bleeding and broken from a multi-story fall), then functional-but-injured
registers.exit: Standing and mobile but limping and in pain; still capable of running and diving for the phone.

registers.entry: Knows only that her line was traced, not how; models the cops as an ordinary, survivable threat.
registers.change: knowledge: ignorant of the hardline cut and the Agents' nature -> learns the hardline is cut (this exit dead) and receives the Wells and Lake phone as the new exit; witnesses an Agent duplicate an impossible jump
registers.exit: Knows her exit is the Wells and Lake phone and that the Agents exceed human limits; still does not know the Agents have already judged the squad dead or that an informant is feeding them.

registers.entry: Cold, trained alertness; compliance as calculation, not fear.
registers.change: emotional: controlled -> briefly frustrated/panicked on learning Agents are present -> re-centered on a given target -> narrowed, will-driven focus through pain
registers.exit: Composed and forward-focused, running on will through a broken body; no panic, no gloating.

registers.entry: Alone in the room; connected to Morpheus/the Operator by phone.
registers.change: relational: isolated captive -> directed by Morpheus (given the exit and the 'Go') -> cut off again as she drops the line and runs
registers.exit: Alone and out of contact, having used the phone network only as an exit, not a lifeline.

registers.entry: Detained suspect under police control.
registers.change: status: captured -> the last one standing over a dead squad -> fugitive -> escaped and unaccounted for
registers.exit: A loose end the Agents believe they can forget; in fact the one who will carry the warning back to the crew.

registers.entry: Arriving to assert federal jurisdiction over a hostile local operation.
registers.change: standing: rebuffed by the Lieutenant -> takes over the operation -> converts a failed capture into the 'Neo' lead and orders a search
registers.exit: In command, having turned Trinity's escape into the initiative; almost smiling, reassured by the informant.

registers.entry: Already knows the squad is dead before the Lieutenant does.
registers.change: knowledge: certain of the squad's death -> confirmed the informant is real and obtains the target name 'Neo' -> sets a search in motion
registers.exit: Holds a concrete, actionable lead and believes the pipeline is sound; does not know the informant is betraying his own crew.

registers.entry: Outside the hotel with Brown and Jones.
registers.change: positional: with the other Agents -> splits to the alley to block the descent -> returns to the street after the truck strike
registers.exit: At the destroyed booth on the street with Jones and Brown, finding no body.

registers.entry: Cold, authoritative, contemptuous of the Lieutenant's confidence.
registers.change: emotional: frustrated at the escape (grinds his molars) -> displaces it with cold satisfaction ('It doesn't matter,' almost smiles)
registers.exit: Recomposed and satisfied, treating Trinity's escape as irrelevant next to the 'Neo' prize.

registers.entry: Arriving with Smith and Jones outside the hotel.
registers.change: positional: outside -> enters the hotel to lead a second unit up through the building -> onto the roof -> pursuing across the rooftops
registers.exit: Back at the street with Smith and Jones after the escape; no longer in pursuit.

registers.entry: One of three Agents asserting jurisdiction.
registers.change: status: entering to close the building -> leads the physical pursuit and demonstrates the Agents' ability to duplicate impossible movement -> confirms the 'Neo' lead
registers.exit: Part of the command group that has regained the initiative with a named target.

registers.entry: Operating on the assumption that physical matching equals containment.
registers.change: knowledge: believes every escape Trinity attempts is one he can replicate -> she escapes by a route (the phone) he cannot duplicate
registers.exit: Has the name 'Neo' and a running search; his model that physical parity guarantees capture has been quietly disproven.

registers.entry: Arriving with Smith and Brown to assert jurisdiction.
registers.change: status: supporting the takeover -> confirms the escape and the informant -> confirms the search is already running
registers.exit: Part of the command group holding the 'Neo' lead with a search underway.

registers.entry: Aware the operation is underway; no independent line shown.
registers.change: knowledge: reports 'She got out' -> confirms the informant is real -> confirms the search has begun
registers.exit: Shares the group's actionable lead and the belief that naming 'Neo' equals being able to catch him.

registers.entry: Alive, dominant, breaching the room and moving to cuff Trinity.
registers.change: condition: confident and in control -> killed (nose exploded, then thrown into another cop)
registers.exit: Dead; the first of the squad Trinity drops.

registers.entry: Lead officer of the arrest, driving the breach.
registers.change: status: in command of the suspect -> dead, his certainty the cause of his death
registers.exit: Dead; his misread of Trinity as 'one little girl' has been paid for.

registers.entry: Armed, in formation, holding Trinity at gunpoint.
registers.change: condition: disciplined and confident -> panicking, firing wild -> all down
registers.exit: All dead; the room is Trinity's alone.

registers.entry: Believe they have a lone, surrendering woman safely contained.
registers.change: knowledge: certainty of containment -> shock that she moves faster than they can track -> (dead)
registers.exit: Dead with their model of the threat fatally wrong; the second unit (sc-006) inherits the pursuit.

registers.entry: Confident his two units are bringing 'one little girl' down and that his men are fine.
registers.change: knowledge: confident his men are winning -> informed by Smith that his men are already dead
registers.exit: Disabused of his assumption of control; his authority over the operation is being superseded by the Agents.

registers.entry: In command of the local operation, hostile to the Agents' claim of jurisdiction.
registers.change: status: resisting the Agents' takeover -> losing operational control as the Agents move to take over
registers.exit: Authority collapsing; the Agents are assuming the operation he believed he had handled.

registers.entry: Off-screen, reached by phone; already knows the hardline was cut.
registers.change: knowledge: knows the exit is compromised -> directs Trinity to the Wells and Lake phone and tells her she can make it
registers.exit: Has re-routed Trinity to a viable exit; no further shown change as Trinity drops the line.

registers.entry: Trinity's commander, reached by hardline.
registers.change: relational: calming and directing a panicked operative -> giving the order to go, ending the contact
registers.exit: Out of contact; his role here was to re-center Trinity and supply the exit.

registers.entry: Off-screen, first point of contact on Trinity's traced line.
registers.change: status: answering the traced call -> patching Morpheus through
registers.exit: Has connected Trinity to Morpheus; no further shown function in the event.

registers.entry: Not stated what the Operator knows beyond fielding the call.
registers.change: unchanged: the scene records only that he connects Morpheus; no knowledge shift is shown
registers.exit: No recorded change; his function is purely to route the call.
registers.unchanged_because: The scene shows only that he puts Morpheus through; no knowledge change is recorded for him.

affects_outside.how: Advances from a contained arrest to a full manhunt: the Agents pivot from capturing Trinity to hunting 'Neo,' with a search 'already begun.' The event hands the narrative its next target and its true protagonist's name to the antagonists.

Spends Trinity's narrow escape to buy the warning that the hardline was cut and that the Agents are active; the crew's position is worsened because the Agents now have a confirmed informant and the name 'Neo,' tightening the net around the whole cell.

Burns an entire squad to establish that ordinary law enforcement cannot contain this world; the second unit that arrives is led by an Agent, marking the transition from a police matter to an Agent operation.

events.turns_on: Trinity's willingness to risk the impossible — the palm-strike that starts the fight, the 40-foot rooftop jump, and the dive through the window — against an enemy that duplicates physical feats but cannot duplicate her knowledge of an exit or her readiness to take the fall.
events.boundary_reason: The opening raid and Trinity's breakout through the hotel, across the rooftops, and out through the phone booth form one continuous chase; it resolves when she escapes and the Agents pivot to their new lead, 'Neo.'

events.title: Neo Is Summoned and Meets Trinity
events.summary: A machine message forces Neo awake and, via a planted white-rabbit signal, overrides his refusal and draws him out of his apartment to a club, where Trinity makes first contact: she confirms she is behind the intrusions, warns him he is watched and in danger, reframes his lifelong search as a hunt for an answer rather than a man, and leaves him with the named question 'What is the Matrix?' and the promise that the answer will find him.
events.action: Neo wakes to a self-typing screen that names him and tells him 'The Matrix has you,' then directs him to 'Follow the white rabbit.' When a real knock answers the machine's last message, he opens his chained door to Choi and Dujour buying an illegal disk; after the sale he reverses his refusal to go out the moment he sees a white-rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket. At the club, Trinity approaches him by name, confirms she was on his computer, refuses to relocate, tells him he is watched and in danger, converts his search for a man into a search for an answer, and vanishes into the crowd as he voices the question 'What is the Matrix?'

registers.entry: Asleep and oblivious, then woken by a computer that behaves impossibly and types messages on its own.
registers.change: Told by the machine that 'The Matrix has you,' then by Trinity that he is watched, in danger, and that his searching has been for an answer not a man; handed the unresolved question 'What is the Matrix?' with the promise that the answer is looking for him.
registers.exit: Informed that larger forces know and direct him, but still without an actual answer — left holding a named question and a promise that it will find him.

registers.entry: Asleep in front of his PC in his own apartment.
registers.change: Pulled out of his apartment and into the night with Choi and Dujour after the white-rabbit signal, then present and standing alone at the club.
registers.exit: Physically removed from his private, controlled space and placed in an anonymous crowd where he is met by Trinity — no longer at home.

registers.entry: Alone; Choi is a customer and Dujour an acquaintance he can decline.
registers.change: Becomes the target of a coordinated summons (machine + signal + people), then the recipient of Trinity's first contact as his designated warner and guide.
registers.exit: No longer solitary — he is now in active contact with the faction that is both hunting and saving him, with Trinity positioned as the one who knows his interior life.

registers.entry: Disoriented and trying to reassert that his world is ordinary and under his control.
registers.change: The awake/dreaming boundary comes unglued ('the room tilts'); at the club he is startled and off-balance, then magnetized, feeling Trinity's words seep into him 'like a drug.'
registers.exit: Alarmed and drawn in at once — his analytical posture overridden by a pull he cannot defend against, yet still wary.

registers.entry: A small-time illegal disk dealer operating from his apartment.
registers.change: Choi briefly treats him as 'my savior' for handing over the disk, but this is a transactional elevation that does not stick.
registers.exit: Unchanged from the event's point of view: the 'savior' label is dropped the moment Choi leaves and is not what this event establishes for Neo.
registers.unchanged_because: Choi's reverence is a momentary effect of receiving contraband and ends with the sale; Neo's real status shift (hunted object -> chosen subject) is carried by the knowledge and relational registers, not by Choi's flattery.

state_triples.reading: Neo is being lured rather than invited; his reversal only after 'the room tilts' and his susceptibility to Trinity's 'hypnotic' voice show the summons bypassing his rational control, so the event moves him from passive, private searching to being actively found.

registers.entry: Off-stage; she has been steering Neo from a distance (the machine message, the planted rabbit).
registers.change: Enters the story in person, walking straight up to Neo across the club, then melts away into the crowd and disappears.
registers.exit: Physically present and then gone, having delivered the warning in person rather than continuing to act from off-stage.

registers.entry: An anonymous woman approaching a stranger at a party.
registers.change: Revealed as 'The Trinity that cracked the I.R.S. D-Base' — a legendary hacker — and positions herself as Neo's warner and guide.
registers.exit: Established as a figure of renown and authority who knows his private life and speaks for the faction hunting/saving him.

registers.entry: Unknown to Neo except as a legendary name; she has contacted him only through his machine.
registers.change: Makes first face-to-face contact, confirms she was the intruder on his computer, and reframes his entire quest.
registers.exit: Now Neo's designated contact and guide — the first human link between him and the world pursuing him.

registers.entry: Already knows Neo, his habits, and that he is being watched.
registers.change: Discloses to Neo that he is watched and in danger and that his search targets an answer, while deliberately withholding what the Matrix actually is.
registers.exit: Unchanged in what she herself knows; she has only transferred selected knowledge to Neo and retained the rest.
registers.unchanged_because: This event adds nothing to Trinity's own knowledge — she arrives already informed and functions as the one who reveals, not learns.

state_triples.reading: Trinity performs a disciplined seduction under time pressure — using name, legend, proximity, and withheld knowledge to make the unknown feel like a homecoming — and her vanishing act preserves her as a guide who pulls rather than explains.

registers.entry: A customer arriving late to buy an illegal disk.
registers.change: Becomes giddy and reverent toward Neo on receiving the disk, calling him 'my savior.'
registers.exit: Unchanged by the event's end: he completes the purchase and leaves; his elevation of Neo is a momentary, transaction-bound reaction that ends with the sale.
registers.unchanged_because: Choi exits the event immediately after the transaction; his 'savior' outburst is a flash of gratitude tied to getting the disk, not a lasting change, and he plays no part in the summons or the Trinity contact.

registers.entry: A buyer who treats the weirdness around Neo as mescaline and jokes 'You don't exist.'
registers.change: No change: he never learns that Neo is genuinely hunted or that the disk is a thread in the operation tracking Neo.
registers.exit: Unchanged — he leaves as ignorant of the real danger as he arrived, still reading everything as drugs and street trouble.
registers.unchanged_because: Choi is a normalcy-anchor for Neo's ordinary world; the event deliberately keeps him blind to the existential stakes, and nothing he learns or does carries past the sale.

state_triples.reading: Choi (and Dujour) are instruments of the summons, not agents of it — their flippancy dramatises the blindness of the world Neo is about to lose, and neither is changed by the event.

registers.entry: At Neo's door with Choi, inviting him out.
registers.change: Persuades Neo past his refusal and pulls him into the night; wears the white-rabbit pin that is the planted signal.
registers.exit: Unchanged by the event's end in any lasting way: she delivers Neo to the club and then drops out of the story, unaware she has been a lure.
registers.unchanged_because: Dujour is the social instrument of a plan she does not comprehend; she has no knowledge, relationship, or status shift of her own, and exits once Neo reaches the club.

registers.entry: Believes she is coaxing a shy guy to have a good time.
registers.change: No change: she never learns Neo is being summoned rather than invited.
registers.exit: Unchanged — she leaves as ignorant of the summons as she arrived.
registers.unchanged_because: The event keeps Dujour unaware that she is a lure; her ignorance is the cover for the signal, and no scene develops her understanding.

state_triples.reading: Dujour is the visible tip of the planted signal — warm persuasion masking a lure — and the event changes nothing in her; she exists to make Neo's departure look voluntary.

affects_outside.what: Advances the pursuit plot: Neo is now in direct contact with the faction the Agents are hunting, and Trinity has warned him he is watched — this tightens the convergence between Neo's awakening and the Agents' widening search set in motion in earlier scenes.
affects_outside.how: The event moves Neo from private, passive searching to being actively found and named, handing him the question 'What is the Matrix?' that the following events must answer; it sets the red-pill choice in motion.

events.turns_on: The white-rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket — the physical answer to the machine's 'Follow the white rabbit' — which is what actually breaks Neo's refusal and sends him to the place where Trinity can reach him.
events.boundary_reason: The story shifts from the Agents to Neo: the machine messages summon him via the white rabbit, and the party confrontation with Trinity ends the beat by posing the unanswered question 'What is the Matrix?'

events.title: Neo's Capture at the Office
events.summary: Woken late into an ordinary workday, Neo is disciplined by his boss, then seized mid-raid on the office floor as Morpheus tries to guide him out. The escape route — across the hall, down a row, out a window onto a ledge — collapses under his terror, and he is taken into custody. In an interrogation room he rejects Agent Smith's deal, whereupon the Agents seal his mouth shut and burrow a wire-tap creature into his body, converting him from a defiant suspect into a physically violated asset.
events.action: The event moves Neo from the insulated routine of his double life into open, physical peril and finally into bodily violation. Rhineheart's ultimatum (compliance or unemployment) is immediately overtaken by a raid: a phone arrives, Morpheus commands, the Agents close, and Neo is shepherded through concealment and a ledge-climb that he cannot complete. He is arrested, and in the interrogation room Smith's offer of a clean slate is refused, triggering the mouth-sealing and the navel-bug. The pursuit that began as a warning ends with the target caught, marked, and claimed.

registers.entry: Late, asleep-just-woken in his apartment, then at his desk in the Meta CorTechs office.
registers.change: From exposed at his cubicle, to concealed and moving through the floor (lunging, freezing, sneaking), to trapped on an exterior ledge, back inside when a cop enters, then handcuffed out of the building into a sedan, and finally strapped into a chair in the interrogation room.
registers.exit: Immobile, restrained in the interrogation-room chair, his body no longer his own.

registers.entry: A subordinate being reprimanded; a man with two lives but still protected by ordinary routine.
registers.change: From disciplined employee to wanted fugitive ('they're coming for you') to captured suspect to physically invaded subject — a fiber-optic creature burrows into his navel.
registers.exit: A marked, claimed asset: Smith states he will be made to help 'whether you want to or not.'

registers.entry: Unaware of any threat; absorbed in the ordinary workday.
registers.change: Learns the Agents are coming for him, sees them leading cops, and is told an explanation is coming; in interrogation, learns his full file is known and that the Agents can alter his body.
registers.exit: Knows the pursuit is real and lethal, but still does not grasp that the Agents are more than ordinary authority — his rights-based framing has just been physically disproven.

registers.entry: Detached from and inwardly resistant to Rhineheart; a stranger to Morpheus and the Agents.
registers.change: Submits verbally to Rhineheart; then places trust in Morpheus's voice and obeys it under fire; then is treated as a target by the Agents and a betrayer by the female employee.
registers.exit: Bound to Morpheus as his only guide, and in open, physical enmity with the Agents.

registers.entry: Annoyed at the time, then detached during the lecture.
registers.change: A fast spike from unnerved to terror under the raid; raw, drowning panic on the ledge; defiant bravado in interrogation that collapses into genuine terror when his body is seized.
registers.exit: Helpless and terrified, his defiance broken by the mouth-sealing and the burrowing device.

registers.entry: Awake, whole, unremarkable.
registers.change: Exhausted by concealment and the failed climb; then his jaw tightens, his lips meld until his mouth is gone, his shirt is ripped open, and a creature burrows into his navel.
registers.exit: Mouthless and internally wired — unable to speak, his body no longer his own.

state_triples.reading: The event is the ordinary world proving it was never harmless: the petty reprimand escalates, without a break, into a manhunt and then into bodily violation, so that Neo's detachment is punished and his self-image as 'nobody' is physically dismantled.

registers.entry: A manager lecturing a chronically late subordinate without looking at him.
registers.change: Escalates from criticism to a direct ultimatum — punctuality or the job — and extracts a verbal submission.
registers.exit: Reasserted as authority in his own frame, having won the encounter.

registers.entry: Believes Neo is an arrogant slacker with an authority problem — a petty disciplinary case.
registers.change: Unchanged: he never learns Neo is the person the real powers are hunting.
registers.exit: Still managing a man on the verge of being pulled out of the very system Rhineheart thinks he is defending.
registers.unchanged_because: He is not present after sc-016, and nothing in the event corrects his misreading; his belief is the event's irony, not a position that changes.

registers.entry: Not applicable beyond sc-016.
registers.change: unchanged: he is not present after the office reprimand.
registers.exit: unchanged: absent from the rest of the event.
registers.unchanged_because: He appears only in sc-016 and does not reappear.

state_triples.reading: Rhineheart embodies the hollowness of the authority Neo is outgrowing — his performative control is immediately shown up as trivial by the real, physical power that follows.

registers.entry: Absent from the floor, present only as a voice on a phone.
registers.change: Guides Neo through the raid and to the window, then forces the ledge choice and hangs up, leaving Neo alone with it.
registers.exit: Still off-site and voice-only; his guidance has failed to get Neo out.

registers.entry: A hidden operator who has been looking for Neo and can read the floor like a board.
registers.change: Attempts a clean extraction of a panicked novice; the plan runs out of time and Neo is captured despite the guidance.
registers.exit: A gambler whose confidence in a clean extraction has been disproven — he could not prevent the capture.

registers.entry: A stranger-voice to Neo; an unseen protector.
registers.change: Becomes the authority Neo obeys under fire, then the one who refuses to soothe him and forces him to choose.
registers.exit: Neo's only guide, but one whose trust now outruns his demonstrated control.

registers.entry: Not applicable — he is only a voice.
registers.change: unchanged: he never appears on-screen in this event.
registers.exit: unchanged: still voice-only.
registers.unchanged_because: He is present only as V.O. and is not physically acted upon.

state_triples.reading: Morpheus's calm, command-not-comfort method works tactically but cannot overcome the Agents' reach — the event establishes both his competence and the limit of his control over Neo's fate.

registers.entry: The organizing presence of the raid, moving cops as pieces with unhurried certainty.
registers.change: From negotiator offering a clean slate in exchange for Morpheus, to openly coercive enforcer once refused.
registers.exit: In full physical control, having sealed Neo's mouth and wired his body — the 'reasonable' mask removed.

registers.entry: Treats Neo as a contained, catchable fugitive — a small-time hacker to be flipped.
registers.change: Moves from paternal persuasion ('you want to do the right thing') to proprietary contempt ('whether you want to or not').
registers.exit: Neo's captor and violator, certain of his own control and blind to what Neo will become.

registers.entry: Believes Neo is a rational, frightenable criminal pliable to deal and fear.
registers.change: Unchanged in kind: his contempt is never corrected within the event; he never suspects 'The One.'
registers.exit: Still operating on a categorical error — mistaking Neo's latent capacity for a small-time hacker's pliability — that the rest of the story will exploit.
registers.unchanged_because: The event confirms his tactical success (he takes Neo) but does nothing to correct his misreading of who Neo is; the flaw is set, not changed.

registers.entry: Not applicable beyond his on-screen actions.
registers.change: Removes and replaces his sunglasses as a signal of the negotiation ending; otherwise physically unchanged.
registers.exit: Physically unchanged; he is the agent of change, not its object.
registers.unchanged_because: He acts on Neo's body but is not himself physically altered.

state_triples.reading: Smith's cold certainty and fatal contempt are the event's counterweight to Morpheus's calm; his pivot from persuasion to force reveals that the 'offer' was always a formality, and his misreading of Neo is the flaw the story will later exploit.

registers.entry: Watching the building, unaware of the outcome.
registers.change: Sees Neo arrested in her rearview mirror and realizes the capture has succeeded.
registers.exit: Aware Neo has been taken; the pursuit has lost its target to the Agents.

registers.entry: Seated on her motorcycle outside the skyscraper.
registers.change: Unchanged: she remains a witness, taking no action within the event.
registers.exit: Still on her motorcycle, having only observed the arrest.
registers.unchanged_because: She does not move or intervene; she only watches and reacts.

registers.entry: Not applicable beyond her reaction.
registers.change: unchanged: she is not physically acted upon.
registers.exit: unchanged: physically whole, only reacting with a curse.
registers.unchanged_because: She witnesses but is not touched by the event's physical action.

state_triples.reading: Trinity is the event's witness and its register of loss — her curse marks that the extraction has failed and the target is now in enemy hands.

registers.entry: An orderly, methodical force closing on a contained target.
registers.change: Sweep the floor, seize Neo, and in the interrogation room physically enforce him — sealing his mouth, restraining him, wiring his body.
registers.exit: In uncontested physical control, having converted persuasion into violation.

registers.entry: Believe Neo is a target to be processed, not reasoned with.
registers.change: Unchanged in kind: their dehumanizing certainty is never corrected within the event.
registers.exit: Still treating Neo as an object to be wired — a category error the story will overturn.
registers.unchanged_because: The event confirms their success but does not correct their misreading of Neo.

registers.entry: Not applicable beyond their actions.
registers.change: unchanged: they act on Neo's body but are not themselves physically altered.
registers.exit: unchanged: physically whole; they are the instruments of change.
registers.unchanged_because: They are the enforcers, not the objects, of the physical violation.

state_triples.reading: The Agents are the event's implacable mechanism — orderly, unhurried, and physically absolute — whose dehumanizing certainty sets up the reversal the story will later deliver.

registers.entry: A search party led by the Agents into the office floor.
registers.change: Sweep the floor, search the bathroom, and one cop opens the door that traps Neo back inside.
registers.exit: Having completed the floor search; one has cornered Neo, enabling the arrest.

registers.entry: Unchanged: ordinary officers executing a search, unaware of the larger stakes.
registers.change: unchanged: they remain instruments of the raid with no corrected belief.
registers.exit: unchanged: still operating inside ordinary law-enforcement logic.
registers.unchanged_because: They are functionaries of the raid; nothing in the event changes their understanding.

registers.entry: Not applicable beyond their search actions.
registers.change: unchanged: they search and corner but are not physically altered.
registers.exit: unchanged: physically whole.
registers.unchanged_because: They act but are not acted upon.

state_triples.reading: The cops are the ordinary-world teeth of the raid — their mundane search function makes the escalation into body-horror feel all the more invasive.

registers.entry: A coworker in the honeycomb, position ambiguous.
registers.change: Turns and points out Neo's cubicle to the Agents, enabling the raid to home in.
registers.exit: Having handed Neo over, receding into the office — either unthinking compliance or knowing betrayal, the scene won't say.

registers.entry: Believes Neo is a troublemaker the authorities are entitled to.
registers.change: Unchanged: she cannot know he is 'The One' or that the authorities are programs.
registers.exit: Still categorizing him inside the system's logic.
registers.unchanged_because: Her misreading is never corrected within the event; it is the system's logic in miniature.

registers.entry: Not applicable beyond her gesture.
registers.change: unchanged: she points and recedes, physically untouched.
registers.exit: unchanged: physically whole.
registers.unchanged_because: She acts but is not acted upon.

state_triples.reading: Her single pointing gesture is the ordinary world's quiet betrayal — the moment a coworker treats Neo as a problem to be handed over, sealing his exposure.

affects_outside.how: The event ends the chase phase: the target Morpheus and Trinity are hunting is now captured and physically marked by the Agents, moving the story from pursuit to revelation/interrogation and forcing the rescuers to respond to a taken, wired asset rather than a free doubter.
Worsened — she witnesses the extraction fail and the target lost to the enemy, cursing; the operation she is part of has taken a hard setback.

Advanced in the short term — he has captured and violated the target against his colleagues' skepticism — but the event also locks in the contempt and categorical error that the rest of the story will exploit against him.

events.turns_on: Neo's failure of nerve on the ledge — the one exit Morpheus offers that Neo cannot complete — which converts a possible clean escape into a foregone capture.
events.boundary_reason: A new situation begins with Neo waking late for work; the office pursuit, failed ledge escape, arrest, and interrogation with the mouth-sealing and bug implant are one captured-and-coerced arc, ending when the bug takes hold and the scene cuts away.

events.title: Neo Chooses to Meet Morpheus
events.summary: Morpheus reaches Neo by tapped phone, names him 'the One,' and re-secures his agreement to meet; Neo commits. The crew then collects him off the street, and, after an armed standoff in the car that Neo tries to bolt from, Trinity's appeal to a road he recognises wins his reluctant trust and he submits to being driven away.

events.boundary_reason: Neo waking from the apparent nightmare resets the situation; he commits to meeting Morpheus, is collected by Trinity's crew, and submits to their custody in the car, launching a new journey whose destination is still ahead.

events.title: The Bug Extraction
events.summary: Trinity and Switch perform a forced extraction that pulls a real surveillance bug out of Neo's body, converting the chase's abstract 'you're being watched' into physical, undeniable proof inside him, and leaving the crew momentarily clean of tracking as the car drives off.

events.title: Arrival and the Choice
events.summary: The car arrives at a forgotten hotel and Neo is led to room 1313, where the legendary figure inside reveals himself as Morpheus. Morpheus names Neo's lifelong unease as the Matrix, explains it as an inescapable mind-prison that cannot be described but only seen, and offers an irreversible choice: a blue pill to return to ignorance, or a red pill to learn the truth. Neo swallows the red pill, committing himself, and Morpheus leads him onward.
events.action: The car stops in a deserted alley behind the Hotel Lafayette; Trinity leads Neo down the thirteenth-floor hallway to room 1313 and warns him the man inside knows more than he can imagine. Inside, Morpheus greets Neo, seats him, names the wrongness he has felt as the Matrix, explains it as a prison that blinds people from truth and cannot be told but must be seen, and offers two pills — blue to end the story and return to ignorance, red to learn the truth. Neo swallows the red pill. Morpheus smiles and says 'Follow me.'

events.turns_on: Neo's free, self-authored choice to swallow the red pill — irreversible truth over comfortable ignorance.
events.boundary_reason: The car reaches the Hotel Lafayette and Neo is led to Morpheus; the whole run builds to and resolves on the single irreversible decision — swallowing the red pill — after which a different question (what happens next) begins.

events.title: Waking the Body
events.summary: The crew hardwires the hotel room on-line and Neo, wired into the trace, is consumed by liquefying mirror matter that drives him into cardiac arrest; the crew fires the extraction signal and his consciousness is pulled through into the real world, where he tears free of his bio-pod, is serviced by a harvester machine that unplugs the skull-cable he could not remove himself, is flushed through the waste-disposal system, is snatched from drowning by a hovercraft's retrieval cable, and is laid before Morpheus — who welcomes him to the real world — before he passes out.
events.action: To complete Neo's unplugging: convert the philosophical promise of the red pill into bodily fact, carry him from the Matrix through the real-world machinery of human harvesting, and deliver him — alive but helpless — into the crew's custody aboard the hovercraft.
locations: POWER PLANT - CLOSE ON MAN'S BODY

registers.entry: Seated, clothed, electrodes being fixed to him by Trinity; awake and merely anxious.
registers.change: Mirror gel invades his body, inducing fibrillation and cardiac arrest; consciousness is pulled through the trace; he then ruptures a magenta amnion, emerges bald and naked, discovers IVs grafted to his flesh and a coaxial cable locked into the base of his skull; a machine detaches the cable, a needle and a cerebrum-chip, and the other hoses; he is flushed through grease traps and nearly drowns in waste before being hauled into the hovercraft.
registers.exit: Stripped, shaved, ungrafted of the machine's connections, and half-conscious on the hovercraft floor — alive but physiologically wrecked, then unconscious.

registers.entry: In the hotel room, seated at the center of the crew's hardwire setup.
registers.change: His target is locked and his signal fired; he is physically relocated from the Matrix into a pod in the real-world power plant, then through the waste line and sewer main, then up into the hovercraft's belly and dropped onto its floor before Morpheus.
registers.exit: Aboard the hovercraft, in the crew's physical custody, face-to-face with Morpheus.

registers.entry: Accepts the physical setup but does not understand the mechanics; asks what the trace program means.
registers.change: His expectation that waking means standing free as a comprehensible man is overturned — the truth is harvest: towers of human-filled pods, himself one grafted unit among them; the abstract 'wrongness' he felt his whole life becomes literal and vast.
registers.exit: Comprehends the scale of the horror — that freedom looks like being harvested — but has no framework yet for rescue-as-violation.

registers.entry: A candidate being unplugged; the crew's job, not yet proven to be 'the one.'
registers.change: Survives a non-routine extraction that goes into replication crisis and arrest; is successfully unplugged and recovered by the crew.
registers.exit: Delivered alive into the real world — a recovered body, not a corpse; his survival is now a fact the coming scenes must interpret.

registers.entry: Handled gently by Trinity; trusts Morpheus as a guide who will explain and protect him.

registers.entry: Anxious, curious, reaching for a witness to confirm the world still makes sense.
registers.change: Mounting wordless terror as his own body becomes evidence against reality; raw physiological panic in the pod; dawning horror at the landscape; helplessness when he cannot pull the cable free; a brief smile of recognition at Morpheus.
registers.exit: Overwhelmed into unconsciousness immediately after the smile.

state_triples.reading: Neo's arc is the conversion of intellectual curiosity into bodily disbelief and then into recovered-but-helpless fact: he does not achieve the unplugging himself — the system that enslaved him performs the act that frees him — so his 'waking' is something done to him, not something he does.

events.title: Recovery and Orientation
events.summary: Neo is brought back from the pod and through the first hours of recovery aboard the Nebuchadnezzar. He is rebuilt physically, then deliberately reoriented out of his one remaining certainty — that he knows what year it is — before being led onto the deck to begin seeing the truth for himself.
events.action: Morpheus and Trinity confirm the rescue is complete as Neo regains consciousness disoriented on the ship. Dozer and Morpheus rebuild his atrophied muscles and explain his eyes hurt because he has never used them, then Morpheus sends him back to rest with the promise that answers are coming. Neo later wakes in his room, discovers outlets grafted into his forearm and skull and his shorn hair, and demands to know what has been done to him and where he is. Morpheus reframes the question from 'where' to 'when,' telling him the year is closer to 2197 than 1997 and that no one knows the exact year, then refuses to explain further and instead offers to show him, leading him dazed through the ship, naming it the Nebuchadnezzar, and climbing toward the main deck.

registers.exit: Physically restored enough to walk, but carrying foreign hardware in his own flesh that he has just found by touch.

events.title: The Truth of the Matrix
events.summary: Morpheus takes Neo to the threshold of the truth and forces him to undergo it rather than hear it. Jacked into the ship's Core on the main deck before the assembled crew, Neo is carried into the Construct, where Morpheus dismantles his faith in the world he knew — revealing the Matrix as a neural-interactive simulation, the real world as a scorched wasteland, and humanity's purpose as a grown power source for the Machines — before Neo's mind rejects the overload and his body ejects him back into the chair in violent physical collapse. The event converts the story from a mystery Neo is chasing into a mission he has been conscripted into, and binds his only remaining certainty to Morpheus as the guide who showed him a truth he cannot yet bear.
events.action: Morpheus gathers the crew on the main deck, introduces Neo to those he has not met, and stages the Core as the place where the truth will be delivered. Against Neo's expectation of a verbal answer, Morpheus feeds a coaxial line with a cerebrum chip into the jack at the back of Neo's neck, jacking him into the ship's network. Neo is carried into the Construct, a blank-white loading program, where Morpheus demonstrates that his body here is only a 'residual self image,' then uses a television to show him the Twentieth-Century city he knew as the Matrix, switches to the ruined present, and descends with him through the screen to the scorched lake bed. There Morpheus recounts the origin of the Machines — mankind's creation of A.I., the war, the scorching of the sky — and shows him the fetus fields where humans are grown as a power source and the power plant where the dead are liquefied to feed the living. Returning to the construct, Morpheus defines the Matrix as 'control' and holds up a coppertop battery as what a human being has become. Neo rejects it — 'No! I don't believe it! It's not possible!' — and, overwhelmed, demands to be let out. He wakes back in the chair on the main deck thrashing to rip the cable from his neck; Trinity calms him while Dozer holds him and the cable is unlocked. Neo tears free, recoils from their touch, reels in vertigo and skull pressure, and vomits before pitching forward and blacking out.

registers.exit: In possession of a complete new cosmology he intellectually cannot yet accept — he rejects it ('It's not possible') and demands out, carrying a truth he has been shown but has not been able to bear.

affects_outside.what: The central mystery of the story — 'what is the Matrix?' — is resolved and the narrative converts from mystery into mission; every subsequent scene now operates on the cosmology established here (simulation, ruined reality, humans as a power source).

events.boundary_reason: Neo is jacked into the Construct and shown what the Matrix and the real world truly are; the explanatory run culminates in his rejection and physical collapse back on the deck, closing the revelation and its immediate aftermath.

events.title: No Going Back / The Prophecy
events.summary: Freshly freed and terrified, Neo asks whether he can return to his old life. Morpheus, waiting in the dark, confirms there is no return, apologizes for having broken a rule against freeing minds past a certain age, and explains why: such minds cannot let go and turn against themselves. He then tells Neo the origin myth of the Matrix—a man born inside it who could remake it, who freed the first of them and taught that no one can be free while the Matrix stands—and the Oracle's prophecy of that man's return, said to bring the Matrix's destruction, an end to the war, and freedom. Morpheus declares that he freed Neo because he believes the search for that man is over, then sends him to rest before training. The scene converts Neo's rescue from a frightening mistake into the fulfillment of a lifelong search, and leaves him a reluctant candidate for a destiny he has not agreed to believe in.
events.action: exposition_as_confession_and_conversion_of_a_fleeing_prisoner_into_a_recalcitrant_candidate

events.title: The Jump Program
events.summary: Morpheus runs Neo through his first jump in the Construct. After demonstrating the leap across a rooftop gap, he leaves Neo to attempt it alone; Neo comes up short and falls, the program's ground stretching to catch him. In the aftermath Neo names the cause of his failure as his own disbelief, and Morpheus confirms he is right. Meanwhile the crew watches the attempt on a monitor, the veterans certain he cannot succeed and Trinity, breaking her silence, quietly hoping that he does.

events.title: The Cost of Dying in the Matrix
events.summary: The crew scatters after the jump program, and as Neo is unplugged, injured and spitting blood, Morpheus converts his assumption that the Matrix is 'not real' into the operative rule that the mind governs the body — establishing that death inside the simulation means death for the body in the real world.

events.title: The Agent Training Program
events.summary: Morpheus walks Neo through a simulated crowded street to teach, experientially, what the Matrix and its Agents are. He frames the Matrix as an enemy system whose inhabited people are part of it, then baits Neo with a woman in a red dress and swaps her for Agent Smith pointing a gun at Neo's face, provoking a scream. Morpheus freezes the simulation and reveals it is a training program, teaching that Agents are sentient programs who can inhabit anyone still plugged in, that they guard every door, and that everyone who has fought an Agent has died — but that Agents are bound by the rules of their world, so Neo can become stronger and faster than them. When Neo asks whether he must dodge bullets, Morpheus reframes the goal as not needing to. The session is cut short when Tank calls through Morpheus's phone to report trouble.

events.title: Cypher's Deal
events.summary: Two linked transactions convert private disillusionment into active treason. First, Cypher isolates Neo and, under the cover of a shared drink, reframes the One-prophecy as a graveyard — five dead predecessors — seeding doubt and positioning himself as Neo's trusted confidant. He then carries that manufactured disillusionment to Agent Smith, where he barters the crew's survival for reinsertion into the Matrix, delivering Morpheus as the price. The event binds the ship's internal rot to the external enemy and sets a concrete countdown in motion.
events.action: Cypher pulls Neo aside on the main deck, shows him the encoded Matrix, gets him drunk, and reveals that Morpheus has found the One five times before — all dead. He then meets Agent Smith in a simulated restaurant, savours an illusory steak, negotiates his terms (erased memory, wealth, importance), and agrees to hand over 'the man who has the codes,' whom Smith names as Morpheus.

registers.change: Moves from private resentment to active conspiracy: he recruits Neo into his cynicism, then brokers a deal with the Machines to betray the crew.

state_triples.reading: Cypher's arc in this event is the externalisation of a private wound into public betrayal. The 'little secret' scene is not kindness — the secrecy clause and the pivot to undermining Morpheus show him recruiting an ally for his despair. When that fails to land on a fervent Neo, he takes the same disillusionment and sells it to the enemy. The steak-savouring is a performance of the life he has chosen: he would rather be comfortably lied to than honestly free.

events.title: Departure for the Oracle
events.summary: Morpheus interrupts the crew's breakfast to take Neo to the Oracle, triggering the ship's transition into the Matrix. The crew jacks in and assembles at the Hotel Lafayette, then drives Neo through the city to the Oracle's building. Along the way Neo confronts the falseness of his memories and the Oracle's meaning, Trinity is overcome when asked what the prophecy told her, and Cypher's hidden betrayal surfaces as he plants a connecting phone and needles Trinity.
events.action: The ship moves from respite into the decisive step of Morpheus's project: delivering Neo to the Oracle. The crew transitions from the real world into the Matrix, and Neo is carried toward the test that will confirm or break the prophecy.

events.turns_on: The transition from the real world into the Matrix and Neo's arrival at the Oracle — the moment Morpheus's prophecy moves from belief into a live test, while Cypher's betrayal simultaneously moves from intent into action.
events.boundary_reason: From Morpheus announcing the Oracle trip, through the crew jacking in and materializing in the Matrix, the car ride, and Cypher's secret phone-drop, this is one journey-and-arrival unit. It resolves when they reach the destination building; the next scene is a mood-setting exterior that opens the approach to the Oracle's floor.

events.title: Approach to the Oracle
events.summary: Morpheus escorts Neo across the Matrix to the Oracle's building and, during the ascent, ties the prophecy to his own life by revealing she told him he would find the One. At the Oracle's door Neo resists crossing until Morpheus confesses he already misread the prophecy over five failed candidates and now asks only for trust; Neo capitulates and the door opens on its own. Awaiting the audience among the Potentials, Neo is taught that reality answers perception, and the spoon begins to bend under his own gaze before the Priestess summons him in.

events.title: The Oracle's Prophecy
events.summary: In the Oracle's kitchen, Neo is told he is not the One but is 'waiting for something,' then handed a prophecy that Morpheus will sacrifice his life for Neo's—forcing Neo to choose which of them dies. The Oracle administers the terror in a measured dose and then antidotes it with a cookie, leaving Neo calm but morally responsible for a death he has not yet had to prevent.
events.action: Administering a prophecy in a measured dose and then antidoting it.

events.action: A glitch in the simulation is detected, named, and interpreted, collapsing the crew's sense of safety from routine extraction into confirmed entrapment.

events.title: The Ambush and Mouse's Death
events.summary: As a helicopter closes on the building, the crew arms itself for a fight while, in parallel, the building's hardline is severed and Mouse is cornered in Room 1313. Trapped against a bricked-up window with no phone line to escape through, Mouse is gunned down, and his body dies on the Nebuchadnezzar's main deck — the trap springs shut and claims its first victim.
events.action: A closing helicopter drives the crew to arm themselves; the building's hardline is cut to seal the exit; Mouse is warned too late, trapped against a bricked-up window, and shot dead, his real-world body dying aboard the ship as Tank watches helplessly.

events.title: The Agents Pinpoint the Eighth Floor
events.summary: As the police sweep the Hotel Lafayette floor by floor, the Agents triangulate the crew's position and converge on the eighth floor. Tank feeds Morpheus the structural layout he needs to move blind inside the building, while Agent Smith, standing over Mouse's body, receives the report that fixes the fugitives on the eighth floor and relays it to the other Agents; Brown takes the order in the stairwell and the police pour onto the target floor.
events.action: A building-wide police search runs in parallel with two coordination threads. Tank loads a structural diagram for Morpheus, then specifies the main wet-wall and guides Morpheus's blind movement through Room 808 turn by turn. Agent Smith stands over Mouse's corpse, raises his earpiece, and — after the line on the other end clicks dead — reports that the targets are on the eighth floor. Agent Brown listens to his earpiece in the stairwell, and a mass of cops floods the eighth-floor hall.

events.title: Morpheus's Sacrifice and Capture
events.summary: An Agent ambushes Neo in the wall-fight; Morpheus intervenes, pins the Agent, and orders Trinity to extract Neo at the cost of his own life. The crew descends into the basement and escapes through the catch basin, leaving Cypher behind in the gas. In the room above, Morpheus fights Smith to a standstill before being overwhelmed by police and taken into custody. The event converts a chaotic escape into a decisive trade: Neo survives and gets clear, Morpheus is captured, and the crew is fractured.

affects_outside.what: The crew's composition and moral state
affects_outside.how: The crew is fractured twice over: Morpheus is captured and Cypher is left behind. Trinity is made to enforce the sacrifice, and Neo is elevated to 'all that matters' against his will — planting the prophecy's logic in the present and setting up the coming debate over whether that bet is worth the cost.

Neo survives but is now bound by a debt he refused — saved at the cost of the man who saved him. This is the first payment on the sacrifice the outline has promised, and it inverts the hierarchy Morpheus asserts here: Neo will soon override the whole crew to go back for Morpheus.

events.boundary_reason: The escape from the Agent — Morpheus pinning Smith so Neo can flee, and the crew descending into the basement — resolves when Morpheus is overwhelmed and taken; the story's question shifts from 'will they get out' to 'what happened to those left behind.'

events.title: The Survivors Regroup and Locate an Exit
events.summary: The survivors break cover one by one and re-establish contact with the ship. Trinity climbs out of a manhole onto the street; Cypher, having crashed a paddy wagon, demands and is given an exit at Franklin and Erie, which he takes alone; Tank then reconnects with Trinity, who is now with Neo. Over the comms Tank confirms Morpheus is alive but being moved to an unknown location, and reveals that Cypher has already been sent to the Franklin and Erie exit, giving the group its route out. The scattered crew is reunited (minus Morpheus) and now has a known way out.

affects_outside.what: The crew's escape from the Matrix
affects_outside.how: The exit sequence is now underway: Cypher is out and the rest are following through the TV repair shop hardline, advancing the crew toward full extraction.
By exiting first and arming himself while the others are still in transit, Cypher advances his plan to act against the crew; the crew's collective safety is now materially worsened.

events.turns_on: Cypher's head start and concealed rifle — he is awake and armed while the rest of the crew is still helpless in transit.
events.boundary_reason: The story moves from planning the escape to executing it — Cypher reaches and enters the TV repair shop, Tank jacks him out, and the others begin crawling through the ringing phone — a single continuous exfiltration that ends the moment Cypher is awake on the deck and reaching for the rifle.

events.title: Cypher's Betrayal and the Crew's Murder
events.summary: Cypher, having survived his own attempt on Tank's life, systematically murders the jacked-in crew of the Nebuchadnezzar — Apoc, Switch, and Dozer — and delivers Morpheus to the Agents, all while taunting Trinity with the crew's helplessness. He is stopped only at the moment of killing Neo by Tank, who rises charred but alive and shoots Cypher down. Simultaneously, Trinity's attempt to reach the ship by phone is severed, forcing her to learn the betrayal remotely and confirm her faith in Neo.
events.action: betrayal_climax_and_faith_test: the crew is stripped to nothing by an insider's defection, and the film's central question (is the Matrix real / can faith summon the One) is staged as a literal life-or-death test.

registers.entry: Standing over the jacked-in crew on the main deck, wearing Tank's operator headgear, armed with a gun.
registers.change: Fires at Tank (misses), then murders Apoc, Switch, and Dozer one by one; advances to Neo to pull his plug.
registers.exit: Knocked flying by Tank's bolt and shot, ending his killing spree and his control of the deck.

registers.entry: Presenting himself as a weary crew member, secretly having chosen the Machines.
registers.change: Openly declares defection: he gave Morpheus to the Agents and chooses the Matrix over the Nebuchadnezzar.
registers.exit: An avowed traitor and murderer, his alliance with the Machines now explicit and irreversible.

registers.entry: Believes Tank is dead ('had an accident') and that no one remains to stop him.
registers.change: Learns Tank is alive when Tank levels a gun at him.
registers.exit: His certainty shattered — the one variable he miscounted (Tank) is the instrument of his end.

registers.entry: Cold, exhausted resentment curdled into entitlement; reframes murder as a transaction.
registers.change: Performs the killings with languid ease, taunting Neo that a 'miracle' must stop him.
registers.exit: Cries 'No!' as his invulnerability collapses under Tank's return.

registers.entry: In control of the ship while the crew lies helpless.
registers.change: Consolidates that control through murder, believing he has won.
registers.exit: Struck down and dispossessed of the ship by Tank's counter-attack.

registers.entry: Presumed dead ('had an accident') after Cypher's earlier lightning bolt.
registers.change: Revealed alive, charred and bloody; levels a gun and fires a bolt at Cypher.
registers.exit: Wounded but functional, having survived and now actively opposing Cypher.

registers.entry: Off-stage, absent from the deck's visible action.
registers.change: Suddenly appears and fires, interrupting Cypher at Neo's plug.
registers.exit: Present and armed, the active force now controlling the deck.

registers.entry: Targeted by Cypher's betrayal (shot, presumed killed).
registers.change: Becomes the crew's avenger, killing Cypher in the same motion that saves Neo.
registers.exit: Aligned against Cypher as an enemy to be destroyed, with no room for parley.

registers.entry: Alive; cries 'No!' as Cypher shoots Tank.
registers.change: Murdered by Cypher (his 'sizzling body' is later stepped over).
registers.exit: Dead — one of the crew erased as a witness to Cypher's deal.

registers.entry: A living, confused crewman reacting to Trinity's accusation.
registers.change: Cypher twists and yanks his neck cable.
registers.exit: Dead, 'severed from his mind,' hands reaching for nothing.

registers.entry: Alive, begging 'Not like this,' forced to be witnessed by Trinity.
registers.change: Cypher slides his hand to her plug and kills her.
registers.exit: Dead, her body severed from her mind.

registers.entry: Jacked-in, helpless, next in line for Cypher to kill.
registers.change: Becomes the object of Trinity's affirmed belief ('yes'); Cypher is stopped before pulling his plug.
registers.exit: Alive but still helpless — saved by another's faith, not his own action.

registers.entry: Unchanged: he remains jacked-in and motionless throughout; the scene registers him only through others' gaze.
registers.change: unchanged: his body undergoes no action of its own — his entire agency is being the test.
registers.exit: Still jacked-in, alive only because Tank intervened.
registers.unchanged_because: Neo lies silent and passive; nothing he does changes — the change is entirely done to him.

state_triples.reading: This is the last moment Neo will ever be this powerless; the 'miracle' Cypher mocks is what his arc is about to become.

registers.entry: Waiting for an unanswered ring, not knowing who is on the line or why.
registers.change: Cypher answers; she learns Tank 'had an accident' and then that Cypher gave Morpheus to the Agents.
registers.exit: Knows the full extent of the betrayal: 'My God. Morpheus. You gave them Morpheus.'

registers.entry: Anxious but composed, tension only from the unanswered ringing.
registers.change: Recoils in shock at Tank's 'accident,' then terror and grief at the murders and Morpheus's betrayal; pleads for Switch.
registers.exit: Compresses everything into a silent, willed 'yes' — faith against fear.

registers.entry: Connected to the ship by phone, able to demand answers.
registers.change: The line is severed; she is cut off from the ship and forced to witness the murders remotely, helpless in her body.
registers.exit: Isolated from the crew's physical fate, her only remaining act being affirmation of Neo.

registers.entry: An active operator-adjacent figure trying to regain contact.
registers.change: Reduced to a passive witness who can only argue and plead, unable to fight.
registers.exit: Her agency narrowed to a single act of belief (the 'yes') that may summon the One.

state_triples.reading: The 'yes' is faith willed against fear, not confirmed knowledge — she underestimates how completely Cypher has convinced himself, which is why argument cannot move him.

registers.entry: Unchanged: not present in any of these scenes; his condition is only reported.
registers.change: unchanged on screen: he does not act or appear.
registers.exit: Delivered into the Agents' hands by Cypher — a change to his off-screen fate that this event establishes.
registers.unchanged_because: Morpheus is not in these scenes; his capture is reported, not shown, but the event changes his off-screen position.

affects_outside.how: Cypher's confession establishes that Morpheus has been handed to the Agents, setting up the next plot (the rescue attempt). The crew's near-total destruction leaves Neo and Trinity as the only ones who can act on it.
Dozer, Apoc, and Switch are dead and Cypher is down; the ship is stripped to Tank (wounded), Neo, and Trinity — a resource depletion that constrains every subsequent scene.
Trinity's affirmed belief is the faith-test that precedes Neo becoming the One; this event is the threshold his survival must cross.

events.turns_on: Whether someone else's faith can save a helpless Neo — tested as Cypher taunts that only a 'miracle' could stop him, answered by Tank's return rather than by Neo's own power.
events.boundary_reason: Cutting between the shop (dead phone) and the deck (Cypher shooting Tank and Dozer, then killing the jacked-in crew), this is one sustained confrontation — the revelation of the betrayal and its bloody climax — that resolves when the revived Tank blasts Cypher off his feet.

events.title: The Crew Regroups and Decides to Rescue Morpheus
events.summary: The survivors of Cypher's betrayal regroup aboard the Nebuchadnezzar, learn that the Agents are torturing Morpheus for Zion's mainframe codes, and — after the crew resolves to kill Morpheus rather than let Zion fall — Neo rejects that fatalism, re-enters the Matrix to rescue him, and is joined by Trinity, who takes command of the suicide mission. Meanwhile the Agents, believing Morpheus defeated, escalate to physical attack and deploy the sentinels, while Smith breaks from the team to pursue his own escape.
events.action: The crew regroups after the betrayal and, rather than accept Morpheus's death, converts grief into a rescue.

registers.entry: Unconscious aboard the ship, plugged in, mind resisting the Agents' intrusion.
registers.change: Injected with serum twice (dosage doubled); his alpha pattern is set to flip from chaotic to ordered, after which he will reveal Zion's codes; later hunched, leaking, twitching, tortured by Smith's grip.
registers.exit: On the verge of breaking; still silent and holding the line, but his body failing and his mind's collapse imminent absent intervention.

registers.entry: Unconscious aboard the ship, plugged in, mind resisting the Agents' intrusion.
registers.change: Held captive by the Agents in the government building, handcuffed to a chair, wired to monitors.
registers.exit: Captive in the Matrix; his physical body remains on the ship while his mind is the battlefield.
